discard_reason: interval 0 carries process start, network build, value-init load, cuDNN autotune and the first collection; it is not the steady-state rate.
note: The rate segment sits below the 1500-step eval cadence, so the measured s/step is the TRAIN phase (collect + BPTT) only; the eval term is added separately from CTRL's own measured t_eval plus the synchronized per-call backup-vs-HardNet delta at the in-loop eval batch. Both projections are reported, mean and max over the measured intervals.

contention_during_measurement.solo_window: steps 0->200 (11:37:45 - 11:44:07). nvidia-smi showed ONE compute app (this arm) until 11:41:46.
contention_during_measurement.pre_contention_caveat: the 0->200 interval also carries process start / net build / value-init load / cuDNN autotune, so 1.911 s/step is an UPPER bound on the solo steady-state rate, not a clean one.
contention_during_measurement.reading: intervals 200->400 (2.150) and 400->600 (1.624) each partially overlapped a short u_prev segment; the spread between them (32%) is larger than any contention signal this window can resolve, so the arm's reference rate is taken as the post-warmup MEAN 1.887 s/step and the >25% degradation test is run against that.

correction_to_part_I_gate_2.why: Part I scaled CTRL's phase decomposition by a per-call ratio measured on a synthetic batch. A real B2 training segment gives 2.11x CTRL's train rate, not 5.77x. The Part I number is superseded by measurement, not by re-registration of the cap.
